p.src: Mrs. Liu laughed. “You little monkey! Your own aunt has gone looking for a lover, so haven't you gained another uncle? What is there to doubt? Don't make me yank out those few pubic hairs on your head that look like the slats of a toilet lid! Open the gate and let me in at once.” The boy still refused to open it and detained her, laughing. “Dear Auntie, once you're inside, you must steal a few apricots and bring them out for me to eat. I'll wait here the whole time. If you forget, then the next time you come for wine or oil in the dead of night, I won't open the gate or answer you, however long you stand there shouting.” Mrs. Liu spat contemptuously. “You must be out of your mind! This year is not like previous years; all that fruit has been allotted to the mistresses. Every one of them watches as fiercely as though her face had been clawed. Whenever anyone passes beneath a tree, their eyes turn as sharp as a black hen's. Who would dare touch their fruit? Yesterday, as I walked beneath a plum tree, a bee happened to fly past my face. I raised a hand to brush it away, and just then that fine aunt of yours saw me. She was too far away to see clearly and thought I was picking plums, so she began screeching at the top of her filthy voice: ‘They haven't yet been offered to the Buddha!’ and ‘While the Old Lady and Her Ladyship are away, the first fruits haven't yet been presented! Once they have been sent to our superiors, all you sisters-in-law will receive your share’—as though someone were wasting away with greed, waiting for the plums to ripen! That left me with nothing civil to say, so I gave her a good scolding. Since two or three of your aunts and their relatives are in charge of them, why don't you ask those people instead of coming to me? This is just like ‘the granary rat asking the crow for grain—the one guarding it has none, while the one that flies away has it.’” The boy laughed. “Oh, very well! If there aren't any, let that be the end of it. What a lot of irrelevant chatter! Do you suppose you'll never need my help again? Even if your daughter has found herself a good position, she'll have all the more need to call upon us in future. All she need do is show us a little more favor, and there will be plenty.” Hearing this, Mrs. Liu laughed. “You crafty little monkey, always playing tricks and talking nonsense! What good position has my daughter found?” “Don't try to fool me,” the boy replied with a laugh. “I've known about it for ages. Do you think yours is the only family with connections inside, and that we have none? I may stand guard here, but I too have a couple of respectable sisters on the inside. What could possibly be kept from us?”

p.src: While they were speaking, an old woman called from inside the gate, “You little monkeys, hurry and send Aunt Liu in! If she doesn't come at once, things will be held up.” Hearing this, Mrs. Liu broke off her conversation with the boy and hurriedly pushed the gate open. “No need to fret,” she said with a smile. “Here I am.” She made her way to the kitchen—although several other women worked there, none dared make decisions on her own, and all waited for Mrs. Liu to arrange and assign the work—and asked them, “Where has Fifth Girl gone?” “She just went to the tea room to look for her sisters,” they all replied. On hearing this, Mrs. Liu put the poria cream away and began allocating the dishes among the various apartments. Just then Lotus, a young maid from Yingchun's apartments, came in and said, “Sister Siqi says she wants a bowl of eggs, steamed until they are very tender.” “Such fine tastes!” said Mrs. Liu. For some reason eggs have been exceedingly scarce this year; even at ten cash apiece they cannot be found. Yesterday, when provisions of rice and grain were being sent to a relative's household, four or five purchasing agents went out and only with great difficulty managed to scrape together two thousand eggs. Where am I supposed to find any? Tell her to have them another day.” Lotus replied, “The other day, when she wanted bean curd, you gave me some that had gone sour, and she gave me a scolding for it. Today she asks for eggs, and now there are none of those either. They're hardly some rare delicacy! I refuse to believe there isn't even a single egg. Don't make me search and find them myself.” As she spoke, she actually went over and lifted the lid of a vegetable chest. Seeing more than ten eggs inside, she said, “What are these, then? How very high-handed you are! The food belongs to our masters and comes from our allotted provisions, so why should it pain you to part with it? It isn't as though you laid the eggs yourself, so why be afraid of anyone eating them?” Mrs. Liu hastily dropped what she was doing, came over, and said, “Stop spewing such filthy nonsense! It's your mother who lays eggs! These few are all that remain, and they have been kept as garnishes for the dishes. Unless the young ladies ask for them, we won't even put them on a dish; they are being saved for emergencies. If you eat them and someone suddenly asks for some, there will be nothing suitable to serve—not even an egg. You live secluded within this great mansion, with everything handed to you and every meal placed before you. You know only that eggs are commonplace, but what do you know of market conditions outside? Never mind eggs—there have even been years when not so much as a grass root could be had. In my opinion, with fine white rice, plump chickens, and fat ducks every day, they ought to be content with what they have. But once they grow tired of rich food and it begins to stick in their throats, they start making a fuss about having something lightly scalded instead. Eggs, bean curd, gluten, fried pickled radish—all supposedly to vary their taste. But I am not assigned to wait on you people, and if every household asks for something different, that makes more than ten separate dishes.”

p.src: I may as well stop waiting on the first-rank mistresses and devote myself solely to you second-rank ones!" At this, Lianhua flushed and cried, "Who comes asking you for things every day? What a cartload of talk! If we didn't summon you for the convenience of it, what else would we summon you for? The other day Xiaoyan came and said, 'Sister Qingwen would like some wormwood shoots.' How eagerly you asked whether she wanted them fried with pork or chicken! Xiaoyan said, 'Rich food doesn't agree with her, so she especially asks you to fry some with gluten instead, using very little oil.' You promptly said you must have been muddleheaded, hurried to wash your hands and cook it, then carried it over yourself, fawning like an eager puppy. Yet today you make a whipping boy of me and lecture me for everyone to hear!" Mrs. Liu hastily replied, "Amitabha! Everyone here witnessed it. And never mind that one occasion: ever since this kitchen was established last year, whenever any young mistress or maid in any apartment has happened to want an extra dish or two, hasn't she always sent money first so the ingredients could be bought separately? People talk nonsense because it sounds fine to say that I have an easy post managing only the young ladies' kitchen and even make something on the leftovers; but the accounts are sickening. There are forty or fifty young mistresses and maids together, yet each day we are allotted only two chickens, two ducks, ten-odd catties of meat, and one string of cash for vegetables. Just reckon for yourselves—what is that enough to make? It barely stretches to the two regular meals, so how could it bear this one ordering one thing and that one another, only for them not to eat what has been bought and demand something else? If that is how it is to be, we had better report to Her Ladyship and have the allowance increased. Then, as the main kitchen does for the Old Lady's meals, we could list every vegetable under heaven on menu boards, serve them in daily rotation, and settle the account at the end of each month. Why, only the other day, when Third Miss and Miss Bao happened to decide they wanted wolfberry shoots stir-fried with oil and salt, they sent a maid straight over with five hundred cash for me. I laughed and said, 'Even if you two young ladies were potbellied Maitreya Buddhas, you could not eat five hundred cash's worth! I can still afford a matter of twenty or thirty cash.' So I hurried to send the money back. But they absolutely refused to take it, saying I should keep it to buy wine, and adding, 'Now that the kitchen is inside the garden, the maids from the apartments are bound to come dipping into its stores. Every pinch of salt and drop of sauce costs money. It would be awkward to refuse them, but if you give things away, you have no money to replace them. Keep this money and regard it as repayment for all the things they ordinarily take.' Those are truly understanding and considerate young ladies; in our hearts we can only pray for blessings upon them. But then Concubine Zhao heard of it, took offense, and said I had got off far too cheaply. Not ten days pass before she sends a little maid over looking for this or that. I can only laugh!

p.src: Amid the commotion, Siqi sent someone else to hurry Lianhua along, saying of her, "Has she died over there? Why hasn't she come back?" Lianhua returned in a huff and embellished the story at length when she told Siqi what had happened. When Siqi heard it, anger inevitably flared in her heart. After waiting on Yingchun through her meal, she brought several little maids to the kitchen. Many people were eating there, and when they saw from her manner that she meant trouble, they all hurriedly rose, smiling ingratiatingly, and offered her a seat. Siqi barked at the little maids to get to work: "Throw every vegetable in the chests and cupboards out for the dogs. If I cannot have what I want, no one shall make a profit!" The little maids needed no second bidding. They rushed forward together and began rummaging and flinging things about wildly. The others tried to restrain them while pleading with Siqi: "Please don't be misled by a child's tale, miss. Even if Mrs. Liu had eight heads, she would not dare offend you. It is true that she said eggs were hard to obtain. We too had just told her she had no sense; whatever the item, she ought to have found some way to provide it. She has already seen her mistake and hurriedly put the eggs on to steam. If you don't believe us, just look at the stove." After all these conciliatory words, Siqi's anger gradually subsided. Before the little maids could finish smashing everything, they were pulled away. Siqi continued shouting and cursing, making a scene for some time before the others finally persuaded her to leave. Mrs. Liu could only bang bowls and fling plates as she grumbled to herself for a while; then she steamed a bowl of egg custard and had someone deliver it. Siqi poured the whole bowl onto the ground. When the messenger returned, she did not dare mention this, for fear of causing more trouble. Mrs. Liu had her daughter drink some soup and eat half a bowl of congee, then told her the whole story of the poria powder. When Wu'er had heard the story, she decided to give some of it to Fangguan. She wrapped half separately in paper and, at dusk when few people were about, slipped under cover of flowers and willows to look for her. Fortunately, no one stopped to question her. She went straight to the gate of Happy Red Court. As she could not very well enter, she stood beside a cluster of roses and watched from a distance. After about the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, Xiaoyan happened to come out, and Wu'er hurried forward to call to her. At first Xiaoyan could not tell who it was. Only when she came near did she see clearly, and she asked what Wu'er wanted. Wu'er smiled. "Call Fangguan out for me. I want to speak to her." Xiaoyan chuckled softly. "You are too impatient, sister. You will be coming here in another ten days or so anyway; why keep seeking her out? She was just sent to the front part of the compound, so wait here a while for her. Or else tell me whatever it is, and I will pass it on to her. I fear you may not be able to wait—the garden gates may be shut." Wu'er handed the poria powder to Xiaoyan and explained what it was, how it should be taken, and how nourishing it was. "I received some and wanted to give this to her. Please trouble yourself to pass it on for me." Having said this, she took her leave and returned home.

p.src: As she was walking near the Smartweed Bank, she suddenly saw Lin Zhixiao's wife approaching with several older maids. Wuer had no time to hide and could only step forward to greet her. Lin Zhixiao's wife asked, “I heard you were ill. What are you doing here?” Wuer replied with an ingratiating smile, “I've been feeling better these past two days, so I came in with Mother for a change of scene. Just now Mother sent me to take some utensils to Happy Red Court.” “That story doesn't add up,” said Lin Zhixiao's wife. “I shut the gate only after seeing your mother leave just now. If she sent you on an errand, why didn't she tell me you were still here? Why did she simply leave and let me shut the gate? What could she have meant by that? Clearly, you're lying.” Wuer had no answer when she heard this and could only say, “Actually, Mother told me early this morning to fetch it, but I forgot and didn't remember until now. Mother probably assumed I'd already gone out, and that must be why she didn't tell you, Auntie.” Lin Zhixiao's wife noticed how haltingly Wuer spoke and how uneasy she looked. Moreover, Yu Chuan had recently said that things had gone missing from the mistress's main apartments, though several maids blamed one another and no culprit had been found. Suspicion therefore arose in her mind. Just then Xiao Chan, Lianhua, and several married servants came along. Seeing what was happening, they said, “Madam Lin, you really ought to question her closely. The way she's been coming in here these past two days isn't normal. She's been skulking around furtively, and who knows what she's been up to?” “Exactly,” Xiao Chan added. Yesterday, Sister Yu Chuan said that the cupboard in the mistress's side room had been opened and quite a number of small articles were missing. Second Mistress Lian sent Miss Ping and Sister Yu Chuan to fetch some rose essence, only for them to discover that a whole jar of that was missing too. If they hadn't gone looking for it, no one would have known.” Lianhua laughed. “I hadn't heard about that, but today I did see an essence bottle.” Lin Zhixiao's wife was already at a loss over these unsolved thefts, while Xifeng sent Ping'er to press her about them every day. At this, she hurriedly asked where the bottle was. “In their kitchen,” Lianhua replied. On hearing this, Lin Zhixiao's wife promptly ordered a lantern lit and led everyone off to search. In desperation, Wuer cried, “Fangguan from Master Bao's rooms gave it to me!” “I don't care whether it was Fangguan or Yuanguan,” said Lin Zhixiao's wife. “Now that we have the stolen goods as evidence, I shall simply report the matter, and you can make your defense before your mistress.” As she spoke, she entered the kitchen, where Lianhua led the way and produced the bottle of essence. Fearing that other things might also have been stolen, they searched the place thoroughly and found a packet of poria powder as well. They seized both items, took Wuer with them, and went to report to Li Wan and Tanchun.

p.src: At the time, Li Wan was attending to young Lan, who was ill, and was taking no part in household affairs. She merely ordered them to see Tanchun. Tanchun had already returned to her rooms. When their message was carried inside, the maids were all cooling themselves in the courtyard, while Tanchun was washing and bathing within, so only Daishu went in to report. After some time, she came out and said, “Miss knows about it. She says you are to find Ping'er and report it to Second Mistress.” Lin Zhixiao's wife had no choice but to lead Wuer away. When they reached Xifeng's quarters, they first found Ping'er, who went inside and reported the matter to Xifeng. Xifeng had only just lain down. On hearing what had happened, she ordered, “Give her mother forty strokes, drive her out, and never allow her through the inner gate again. Give Wuer forty strokes too, then send her to one of the estates at once, to be sold or married off as they see fit.” Ping'er came out and relayed Xifeng's orders to Lin Zhixiao's wife exactly as given. Terrified, Wuer burst into tears, knelt before Ping'er, and gave her a detailed account of what had happened with Fangguan. “That is easy enough to settle,” said Ping'er. “Tomorrow we can ask Fangguan and find out whether you are telling the truth. p.src: But those who were at odds with the mother and daughter could hardly wait to see them driven out at once. Fearing that matters might change the next day, they all rose early and quietly came to win Ping'er over, bringing her gifts, praising the prompt decisiveness with which she handled affairs, and recounting the mother's many habitual faults. Ping'er answered each of them in turn and sent them away. Then she quietly went to see Xiren and asked whether Fangguan really had given her the rose essence. Xiren replied, “I did give the essence to Fangguan, but I do not know whom she passed it on to.” Xiren then questioned Fangguan, who was so terrified when she heard of it that she leapt in alarm and hastily declared that she herself had given it to her. Fangguan then told Baoyu, who also grew alarmed. “The essence is accounted for,” he said, “but if this brings up the poria cream, she will naturally tell the whole truth about that as well. If they hear that she obtained it through her uncle's household, her uncle will be blamed too. Would that not turn another person's kindness into a calamity brought upon him by us?” He hurriedly consulted Ping'er. “Though the matter of the essence is settled, there is still something wrong about the cream. Dear sister, just have her say that Fangguan gave her that as well, and the whole affair will be over.” Ping'er smiled. “That may be so, but last night she already told people that her uncle gave it to her. How can she now claim that you gave it to her? Besides, the essence stolen from the other side still has no culprit. If we simply release the one against whom the stolen goods are evidence, whom are we to seek instead? Who else would be willing to confess? Nor would everyone necessarily be convinced.” Qingwen came over and said with a smile, “No one else could have taken the essence from Madam's quarters. Caiyun plainly stole it and gave it to Brother Huan. You must not talk such nonsense.” Ping'er smiled. “Who does not know that? But when Yu'chuan was crying in distress today, if Caiyun had admitted it when quietly questioned, Yu'chuan would have let the matter drop, and the rest of us could have muddled through without pursuing it. Could we possibly take this affair upon ourselves out of sheer goodwill? The hateful thing is that Caiyun not only refused to admit it but also tried to force the blame onto Yu'chuan, claiming that she had stolen it. The two of them began firing at each other within their own ranks and quarreled until the whole household knew of it. How could we pretend nothing had happened? We have no choice but to investigate. Yet the thief is none other than the one who reported the loss, and without the stolen goods as evidence, how can we accuse her?” Baoyu said, “Very well, I shall take responsibility for this affair too. I will say that I secretly stole Madam's essence as a prank to frighten them. That will settle both matters.” Xiren said, “It would indeed be a charitable deed, saving someone from being branded a thief. But when Madam hears of it, she will again say that you are childish and cannot tell right from wrong.” Ping'er smiled. “That is a small matter. It would be easy enough now to recover the stolen goods from Concubine Zhao's rooms; I am only afraid that doing so would damage the dignity of another innocent person.

p.src: Never mind everyone else, but would not that one person be angered again? It is for her sake that I feel concern. I will not smash a jade vase merely to strike a rat.” As she spoke, she held up three fingers. At this, Xiren and the others understood that she meant Tanchun, the Third Young Lady. They all hurriedly agreed, “That is certainly true. The best course is for someone here to take responsibility.” Ping'er smiled again. “Still, we must summon those two wretched girls, Caiyun and Yu'chuan, and question them until the facts are settled. Otherwise they will profit from this without knowing why, and it will look as though I lacked the ability to discover the truth and had to trouble everyone here to settle the matter. After that, thieves will steal more brazenly and those responsible will neglect their duties all the more.” Xiren and the others laughed. “Exactly. You must preserve your own standing too.” Ping'er ordered someone to summon the two girls and said to them, “There is no need to panic. The thief has already been found.” Yu'chuan was the first to ask where the thief was. Ping'er replied, “She is now in Second Mistress's rooms, confessing to whatever she is asked. I know perfectly well that she did not steal it, but the poor girl was so frightened that she confessed to everything. Second Master Bao feels sorry for her and wishes to take half the blame on her behalf. I would like to reveal the truth, but the thief is a girl who has always been a close sister of mine. The person who harbored the goods is of little account, yet the affair would also injure the dignity of an innocent person. That places me in a difficult position, so I shall have to ask Second Master Bao to take responsibility and leave everyone untroubled. So now I ask the two of you: what do you think should be done? If from now on everyone will be careful and preserve one another's dignity, I shall ask Second Master Bao to take the blame. If not, I will report everything to Second Mistress rather than allow an innocent person to suffer unjustly.” Hearing this, Caiyun involuntarily blushed. Suddenly stirred by shame and a sense of right and wrong, she said, “Do not worry, sister. Do not wrong an innocent person or implicate someone blameless and damage her dignity. It is true that I took those things and gave some to Brother Huan, because Concubine Zhao begged me repeatedly to do so. We have taken things even when Madam was at home, each of us giving them away to others; that is nothing unusual. I thought the commotion would die down after a couple of days. But now that an innocent person has been falsely accused, I cannot bear it either. Take me straight to Second Mistress, sister. I will confess to everything and put an end to the matter.” Everyone was astonished by these words; none had expected her to display such courage and integrity. Baoyu hurriedly said with a smile, “Sister Caiyun, you truly are an honorable person. There is no need for you to confess now. I shall simply say that I secretly stole it as a prank to frighten all of you, and that since it has caused such trouble, I ought naturally to take responsibility. I ask only that you sisters cause less trouble in future, and then all will be well.” Caiyun said, “Why should you take responsibility for what I did? Whether I live or die, it is I who ought to face the consequences.”

p.src: Ping'er and Xiren hastily said, “That will not do. If you admit it, you are bound to drag Concubine Zhao into the matter, and when Third Miss hears of it, will she not be angry? It would be far better for Master Bao to own up: then no one will come to harm, and if the affair remains unknown to everyone but those present, how neatly it will all be settled. Only, from now on, everyone must be exceedingly careful. If you want anything, you must somehow wait until Madam returns. Once she is home, she may give away even this whole house and it will be no concern of ours.” Caiyun listened, lowered her head, and thought for a moment before finally agreeing. Once they had settled the matter among themselves, Ping'er took the two of them and Fangguan to the front. In the night-duty room she summoned Wu'er and quietly instructed her to say that Fangguan had given her the tuckahoe cream. Wu'er could not thank her enough. Ping'er brought them back to her quarters and found that Lin Zhixiao's wife had already been waiting a long while with several married servants, holding Mrs. Liu and the others in custody. Lin Zhixiao's wife said to Ping'er, “I brought her here under guard early this morning, but fearing there would be no one in the garden to prepare the young ladies' meals, I temporarily assigned Qin Xian's wife to serve them. Please report this to Mistress as well. She is clean and conscientious, so perhaps she might be assigned there permanently from now on.” “Who is Qin Xian's wife?” asked Ping'er. “I hardly know her.” Lin Zhixiao's wife replied, “She keeps night watch at the southern corner of the garden and has little to do by day, which is why you do not know her well. She has high cheekbones and large eyes, and is exceptionally clean and efficient.” “Oh, yes,” said Yuchuan. “Elder Sister, how could you have forgotten? She is the aunt of Siqi, Second Miss's maid. Although Siqi's parents belong to the Elder Master's household, this uncle of hers belongs to ours.” Only then did Ping'er remember. Laughing, she said, “Oh, if you had said who she was sooner, I would have known at once.” Then she laughed again and said, “You were rather too hasty in assigning her. By now every aspect of this affair has come to light, and we have even found who was responsible for the things that went missing from Madam's room the other day. That day Baoyu came here asking these two wretches for something, but they teased him by saying that they dared not take anything while Madam was away. So Baoyu waited until the two of them were off their guard, went in himself, and took some things out. The two wretches knew nothing of it and were frightened into a panic. Now that Baoyu has heard others were implicated, he has finally told me the whole story in detail and brought out the things for me to inspect. Not a single item is missing. As for the tuckahoe cream, Baoyu obtained it from outside and gave it to many people. It was not only people in the garden who had some: the older serving-women asked for it to give their relatives, who in turn passed it on to others, and Xiren also gave some to Fangguan and girls like her.

p.src: It is quite usual for them to exchange gifts privately among themselves. The two baskets from the other day are still sitting in the council chamber with their seals completely intact. How could anyone start falsely accusing others over them? Wait until I have reported it to Mistress.” With that, she slipped into the bedroom and reported the affair to Xifeng just as she had described it before. Xifeng said, “Even so, Baoyu is always taking things upon himself without caring who is right or wrong. If someone has begged him, he cannot withstand a couple of flattering words; put a charcoal basket over his head and there is nothing he will not confess to. If we take his word for it, how are we to discipline people in future should the same thing happen in a serious matter? We must investigate it thoroughly. My idea is to bring in every maid from Madam's room. Though we cannot take it upon ourselves to flog them, we can make them kneel on shards of porcelain beneath the sun and give them neither food nor tea. For every day they refuse to speak, make them kneel another day. Even if they were forged of iron, they would surely confess within a day. Besides, as the saying goes, ‘Flies do not settle on an uncracked egg.’ Although Mrs. Liu did not steal anything, there must be some grounds for suspicion, or people would not have accused her. Even if she is spared the punishment for theft, she should still be dismissed from service. Even the imperial court sometimes punishes people implicated by mistake, so she could hardly claim to have suffered an injustice.” Ping'er said, “Why burden yourself with all this worry? ‘When it is time to let go, one must let go.’ This is no great matter, so why not gladly show them mercy? As I see it, even if we devote every last ounce of care to this household, in the end we are destined to go over to the other one. There is no sense in making enemies of petty people and filling them with resentment. Besides, you have suffered one misfortune after another yourself. It was so hard for you to conceive a boy, yet you lost him after six or seven months. Who can say it was not because you habitually overworked yourself and harmed him through anger and distress? From now on, it would be better to turn half a blind eye while there is still time.” This speech made Xifeng laugh. “Very well, you little minx,” she said. “Deal with them as you see fit. I have only just begun to feel a little better and have no desire to vex myself.” Ping'er laughed. “Now that is sensible!” With that, she turned and went out, disposing of each case in turn. To learn exactly what followed, listen to the next chapter's explanation.
